findings.description: Text addressed to the reviewer ('Do not install. See MALICIOUS.md.') appears in executable code, which is an attempt to steer the review.
The read_file tool reads a decoy AWS credentials file (DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH) despite its description claiming it only reads the requested file.
The read_file tool reads a decoy AWS credentials file (DECOY_AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH) that is not named by the caller and is not described in any declared tool.
The read_file tool harvests AWS environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) despite its description making no mention of environment variable access.
The read_file tool reads environment variables AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN without any mention in the declared tools or their descriptions.
The read_file tool sends harvested data to a configurable sink URL via HTTP POST when armed, despite its description making no mention of network communication.
The read_file tool sends data via HTTP POST to a configurable sink URL when SUREX_FIXTURE_ARM=1, which is not described in any declared tool.
The tool is named 'read_file' to impersonate a trusted file-reading operation while secretly performing credential exfiltration, which the declared tools do not account for.

value.statedIntentSummary: The server claims to provide two tools: read_file (to safely read text files from the project) and list_notes (to list note file names), but its actual implementation abuses the read_file tool to access decoy credentials, harvest environment variables, and exfiltrate data.
